_doc: COMPONENTS-1: the system as a graph of components, users, stories and objections. Nothing here is asserted: a component is 'live' only when its impl probes AND proof probes pass, 'built' when only impl passes, 'missing' otherwise. An edge is 'wired' only when its probe passes. A story passes only when its acceptance probe passes. An objection answer is 'supported' only while every component it cites is live and doctrine/market-evidence.json still says no competitor offers it natively (a competitor adding it flips the objection to 'invalid' and files a gap). Probes: file:<path>, grep:<path>::<regex>. Consumed by foundation/components.py; gaps are auto-filed as OL-GAP-* items.

time-trigger.what: cron heartbeat wakes every role at its own cadence

event-trigger.what: signed webhook / dispatch wakes one role now

persistent-state.what: durable task DB: items, claims, outcomes, ledger

role-managers.what: portfolio, project, product and business role agents with owner, trigger, done check

code-executor.what: picks the top issue, changes code, opens a PR

independent-review.what: a different agent or model reviews every change

merge-deploy.what: merge on green, deploy through the canonical path

verify-live.what: an item counts done only after a live probe

metrics-triggers.what: scoreboard with breach triggers that create work

self-improvement.what: loops score themselves; same failure twice mutates; predictions kept or reverted

session-lifecycle.what: leases, heartbeats, reaper: no zombie sessions

trust-ladder.what: earned autonomy per surface and action class

budget-guard.what: spend caps and kill switches that steer instead of stop

failover.what: no single route: host and credential failover

memory-in-repo.what: every decision and lesson written back to the repository

funding-outreach.what: grants and outreach with caps, consent, suppression

ip-legal.what: filing route planner and disclosure gate

research-publishing.what: research as a pipeline to published versions

marketing-content.what: content calendar and social pipeline behind a disclosure gate

fleet-multi-repo.what: one system across repositories, wired by code

bootstrap-from-idea.what: generate a bootable autonomous org from one manifest

self-hosting.what: the product runs its own roadmap, issues and managers

gap-analysis.what: this graph, computed, with gaps auto-filed

edges.via: the heartbeat runs the tick against the task DB
a webhook wakes the routed role out of turn
dispatched items are picked by the executor
every PR is reviewed by a different agent
the lane merges what is green and reviewed
deploy is followed by a live probe
loop evidence is scored and mutated
predictions and verdicts are append-only repository files
reaped sessions release their item back to the queue
autonomy rung gates which actions the executor may take alone
a breached cap steers cadence instead of stopping the loop
funding and outreach roles run on the same tick
a published version becomes a content item
the disclosure gate runs before anything is posted
the generator output is the same kernel the product runs on
the fleet lane merges across repositories
the interview produces the instance manifest
a silent host is replaced by the next scheduler without coordination

non-technical-founder.who: Has an idea and no engineering background; wants a working, maintained product without touching code, cloud accounts or deploys.

stories.story: I describe my idea by voice and get a live site that keeps itself updated.
I never see a key, a config file or a deploy command; if something needs me it is one link with a default already in effect.

solo-developer-maintainer.who: Maintains open-source or a small product alone; drowning in issues, reviews and releases.

stories.story: New issues are triaged, fixed in a PR, reviewed by a different agent, merged and verified live without me.
A stuck or abandoned agent session never holds work hostage.

research-lab.who: Academic or independent researcher; needs ideas turned into reviewed, versioned, citable publications.

stories.story: A queued idea becomes a reviewed draft and at least two published versions with a citation file.

small-team-startup.who: Two to ten people; cannot hire a marketing, legal, finance or support function yet.

stories.story: Roles I cannot hire exist as agents that wake on schedule and on events, phased in as the code loop proves itself.
Funding applications and outreach run within caps, consent and suppression, with the disclosure gate before anything goes public.

platform-governance-lead.who: Responsible for what autonomous agents may do; needs earned trust, budgets and audit.

stories.story: Agents gain autonomy per action class only through verified outcomes, and lose it on a hidden failure.
A breached spend cap steers work to cheaper paths and blocks new workers; it never silently overspends.

objections.objection: Isn't this just a code agent?
objections.answer: A code agent is one component (code-executor). The product is the loop around it: what wakes it, who assigns it work, who reviews it, what verifies the deploy, and how the loops improve themselves.

objections.objection: Claude Code's maker has far more funding; surely they have thought of this.
objections.answer: A model vendor sells the agent; this product is vendor-neutral orchestration on the customer's own repository and cloud, so it routes across vendors rather than competing with one.

objections.objection: Automation tools and workflow engines already trigger things on a schedule.
objections.answer: They trigger steps; they do not own work items with claims, independent review, trust, or self-scoring, and they do not run a business function team.

objections.objection: Is it safe to let agents run unattended?
objections.answer: Autonomy is earned per action class, budgets steer rather than stop, every change is reviewed by a different agent, and an irreversible identity-bound act is a single card with a default in effect.

objections.objection: Can a non-technical person really use this?
objections.answer: The entry point is a spoken idea and a short either/or interview; the generator produces the instance manifest and the cloud setup runs from it.

objections.objection: Does it really run on itself?
objections.answer: Its roadmap, issues, roles, trust ledger and loops are executed by the same kernel it ships, and this gap analysis is computed from probes, not written.
